newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds close mixed, labor rules impress.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds close mixed, labor rules impress.

text.p: Argentine bonds closed mixed Wednesday with the market pleased by the government's drive to introduce more flexible labor laws.

"We think the strength of the market is coming from the firm government stand on labor flexibility, and also the support from the International Monetary Fund," a trader said, "At the moment we don't see much risk in Argentina."
But he predicted stocks may outpace bonds in coming days.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.40 to $118.90, but Argentina's FRB due 2005 fell $1/8 to 84-1/4.

Trading started in a cheerful mood, with the market still basking in Argentina's successful global bond placement. More good news came from U.S. construction spending figures, which were up 0.9 percent in August.

"The Previsional 2 hit $119. Peso bonds were strong and the stock exchange was up. But at about 1500 local (1800 GMT) a round of profit taking set in," another trader said, "There had been a big rise from yesterday," one trader said.
He said he expected both bonds and stocks to perform well in coming days, and that the spread between peso-denominated and dollar-demoninated bonds should narrow.
"There isn't any justification for a three-point spread," he said.
The market was fairly pleased with the global bond. The $1.0 billion bond was placed at 445 basis points above the U.S. 10-year Treasury note, yielding 11.2 percent.
"The yield was more or less what was expected. The new bond was being traded today," a third trader said.
Interbank call money closed up at 7.0 percent, from 6.8 percent at close Tuesday.
